blocking.issue: encode_public_document is the single public producer entry point and emits the caller's payload dict verbatim, with no allowlist, validation or projection, despite a docstring that claims the opposite. The author-frozen rule is that producers serialize only explicit allowlisted fields and never arbitrary caller dictionaries.
blocking.location: src/ptest/contracts.py:1889-1916 (specifically :1908 "data": data and :1907 "domain": domain), PublicDocument:1867-1886 (data is accepted as any dict), tests/ng/test_contracts.py:993 and :1028-1030 versus :1074-1079
blocking.evidence: encode_public_document's body validates only kind, error/data exclusivity and the types dict|None; it then places the caller dict into the envelope unchanged. Design line 248 states verbatim: "Producers serialize only explicit allowlisted public fields, never arbitrary caller dictionaries or internal records" and "This includes unknown argv/env-like fields". The committed test proves the leak: tests/ng/test_contracts.py:993 sets where["future_top"] = {"argv": [sentinel], "env": {"K": sentinel}}, line 1030 calls C.encode_public_document(kind, data) and asserts only that the document decodes; the sentinel assertion at :1074-1079 is applied to a RE-encode of already-decoded (projected) data, so the bytes returned by the FIRST encode contain "argv":["smuggled-additive-4d7"] and no test can fail. Nothing else closes the gap: T0 exports allowlisted producers only for run (serialize_run_result:1188) and init (serialize_init_result:1560, summarize_config:575). For plan/where/status/history/doctor/register there is no exported producer at all, and the correct converters (_command_dict:1232, _capability_dict:1258, _lease_dict:1335, _finding_dict:1320, _readiness_dict:1311, _obligation_dict:1355, _scan_limits_dict:1367, _scan_usage_dict:1382, _effective_limits_dict:1414) are underscore-private, so T8/T11 must either touch privates or hand-assemble payloads that this encoder will publish unchanged. Concrete failure: a T11 where/status producer that carries a raw config or prepared-run field (e.g. data["launcher"] or data["env"]) publishes it to `--json` stdout and into the --result-json artifact, and the frozen barrier has no check and no possible failing test.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Plan Task0 line 108-109 makes T0 own "Serialize explicit allowlisted public fields, not asdict on a transient argv/env record" and requires that "No known public object island may remain untyped for a later task to invent"; the addendum contract 5 (design line 248) puts the allowlist duty on producers. The report's own contract_notes concede the deviation ("encode_public_document validates kind/shape/exclusivity only ... producer-liberal"), which is a worker choice, not the author's ruling. Leaving the producer side unenforced defers the privacy boundary to unwritten T11/T8 code, which is exactly what this barrier exists to prevent, and repairing it after wave 1 starts is a cross-task shared-contract repair.
blocking.fix: Make the producer boundary enforce the allowlist inside contracts.py: in encode_public_document (and/or PublicDocument.__post_init__), run the payload through the existing authority - _PAYLOAD_VALIDATORS[kind] then _PROJECTORS[kind] - so a success document is always exactly the descriptor field set, and/or export allowlisted per-kind serializers for the six kinds that have none. Add a producer test that passes a payload carrying extra argv/env-like keys to encode_public_document and asserts the emitted JSON key set equals the descriptor field set (not merely that a re-encode of the decoded document is clean).

blocking.issue: The private control-frame and launch-manifest codecs accept unknown fields silently at every level, while the approved design requires the private protocols to be strict and reject unknown fields; the report asserts they "remain strict".
blocking.location: src/ptest/contracts.py:2856-2883 (decode_control_frame reads only protocol/run_id/nonce/kind/payload), :1769-1821 (_require_frame_keys requires keys but forbids extras only for parent-closing at :1784), :2948-3011 (_build_domain/_build_grant/_build_prepared index known keys only), :3031-3049 (decode_launch_manifest); design line 248
blocking.evidence: Design line 248 states: "Private control/launch/bridge protocols remain strict and reject unknown fields; their execution authority is not governed by public forward compatibility." decode_control_frame never compares obj's key set against the five required names, and _require_frame_keys only loops over the required tuple per kind, so a frame such as {protocol:1, run_id, nonce, kind:"cancel", payload:{"signal":15, "escalate_after_s":0}, "extra":...} is accepted and the unknown fields are silently ignored (payload is even copied wholesale into ControlFrame.payload at :1766). The manifest side is the same: _build_prepared:2977-3008 pulls argv/cwd/env_updates/report_path/capability/summary and ignores anything else; decode_launch_manifest:3039-3046 ignores unknown top-level manifest keys. Concrete failure: this is the channel that carries execution authority between the T11 caller and the T7 guard. Under version skew or a shared-barrier mistake, a caller that adds a semantically meaningful field (an extra timeout, a signal-escalation flag, an extra grant field) gets silent acceptance and divergent behavior from the guard, exactly where design line 202 requires that "Protocol enum/field changes require a shared barrier repair, not an independently guessed T7/T11 message".
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Task0 owns and freezes the private protocol descriptors before T7/T11 consume them, and the addendum's fifth frozen contract is the public-drops/private-rejects asymmetry. The report's addendum dan_passes and the acceptance line "private protocols untouched" present this strictness as verified when the codecs do not implement it; the asymmetry the author froze therefore does not exist in the submitted bytes.
blocking.fix: Reject unknown keys in the private codecs: compare the decoded frame's key set against {protocol, run_id, nonce, kind, payload} and each payload's key set against the exact per-kind field list in _require_frame_keys (PROTOCOL_V1_DESCRIPTOR:3498-3512 already catalogues them), and do the same for the manifest object, domain, grant and prepared-run records (PROTOCOL_V1_DESCRIPTOR:3519-3522). Add a negative per level asserting protocol-mismatch for a frame, a payload, a manifest and a prepared-run entry carrying one extra field.

Deviation, not a required finding: run.command carrying literal argv/env keys is a hard rejection (:2340-2341) while the author's rule for same-major additive unknowns is to drop them recursively. The report discloses this deliberately (addendum discovered_not_fixed). I could not construct a failure with a conforming producer - no allowlisted producer emits those names, and rejecting is fail-closed - so I am not requiring a change; the residual risk is that a legitimate future 1.x additive field named argv or env would break same-major compatibility for exactly two names while every other unknown drops. Worth an author confirmation rather than a code change.

Problem messages on the public decode path still interpolate caller-supplied document values: _check_closed:2321 (f"... has unknown value {value!r}" over an arbitrary-length string from the document), _validate_register_payload:2475 ({action!r}), decode_public_document:2755 ({kind!r}, which can be an arbitrary JSON object whose repr is echoed), _check_reason_dict:1972 ({key!r}), decode_control_frame:2871 ({kind!r}). encode_public_document copies message verbatim into the public error field (:1911). Design line 146 says Problem "carries no raw exception text/argv or arbitrary details". This is the public-side remnant of the class fixed on the private side by T0-6; the leaked content originates from the document the caller supplied rather than from private argv, so the harm is bounded to unbounded-size echo of untrusted input into the error document. Not blocking, but cheap to close with fixed messages while the contract is open.

I am not requiring a generator or framework; deriving the validator/projector field sets from the same constant that builds the schema properties would remove the drift surface if the author wants it later.
